Write a pyramid as a set of shard files

Source: R/set.R
a5_write_pyramid_set.Rd

Builds the pyramid of a5_pyramid() and writes it as a pyramid set: a directory of small pyramid files, shards, and an index, set.json. Use it where one file would be too large to open in a browser. A browser reads a file's whole footer before it draws anything, and the footer grows by a few hundred bytes a tile, so a single file of 150 million leaves has a footer of about 20 MB. In a set, a view opens only the few shards around it.

Usage

a5_write_pyramid_set(
  x,
  dest,
  ...,
  lods = NULL,
  tiers = NULL,
  aggregate = c("mean", "rep_child"),
  reducers = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  types = NULL,
  rep_sd = NULL,
  codecs = NULL,
  storage = NULL,
  weights_type = NULL,
  index = c("json", "parquet"),
  compression = c("snappy", "zstd", "none"),
  metadata = NULL,
  threads = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with one a5R::a5_cell column, an a5R::a5_cell vector, or Arrow data with one uint64 column of cells: an Arrow Table, RecordBatch, RecordBatchReader, Dataset or query from the arrow package. The cells must share one resolution and appear once each; rows with NA cells are dropped. An a5R::a5_covering holds cells at mixed resolutions: convert it with a5R::a5_uncompact() first. Arrow data is read into the engine batch by batch without passing through R, so a Dataset over Parquet files (from arrow::open_dataset()) builds without R holding the leaves.

dest

Directory to write the set to. It must not exist or be empty, so a set never mixes with another's files.

...

<tidy-select> Value columns to carry into the pyramid. Default: every numeric column other than the cells. For an Arrow Dataset that includes its partitioning columns, such as year from year=2025/ directories, so name the value columns there.

lods

Integer vector of the coarser LODs to build. Default: every LOD the tiers hold below the leaves, or, without tiers, every resolution from 2 up to the leaves'.

tiers

A data frame with one row per tier and columns lod_min and lod_max (the tier's LODs, inclusive), shard_resolution (from 0 up to lod_min), and optionally tile_size (default 16384) and row_group_size (default NA, one tile a row group; see a5_write_pyramid()). Between them the tiers must hold every level, the leaves included, and each must hold at least one. Default: a5_pyramid_set_tiers().

aggregate

The reducer for every value column: "mean" (default) or "rep_child". See "Reducers".

reducers

Named character vector of reducers for single columns, overriding aggregate, such as c(count = "sum", class = "mode").

weights

Name of a numeric column of non-negative leaf weights for "mean", "mode" and "rep_child", such as the npix column from a5px::a5_read_raster(). NA weights count as 0, and leaves with weight 0 do not count. Default NULL: every leaf counts once.

types

Named character vector of storage types for single columns, such as c(red = "uint8", ndvi = "float32"). See "Column types".

rep_sd

Named numeric vector of standard deviations for "rep_child" columns, such as c(red = 60, green = 60). Default NULL: each column's standard deviation over the leaves, or 1 where that is 0 or undefined (a constant column). That depends on every leaf, so pyramids built from different parts of a region choose representatives differently even where their cells are the same; fix the standard deviations (from a whole-region build's a5_pyramid_info()$columns$sd, say) for builds whose cells must agree.

codecs

Named character vector of codecs for "mean" columns whose values are codes, such as c(embedding = "aef"). See "Codecs". Default NULL: every column stores its values.

storage

Named character vector of how to store vector columns: "fixed_binary" (default), one fixed-length binary value a row, the smallest footer and the fastest decode; or "list", a Parquet list of the elements, dictionary encoded, which engines such as DuckDB read as an array column (TINYINT[]), as the a5embeddings store keeps its embeddings (format version 4). Such as c(embedding = "list").

weights_type

NULL (default), or a storage type (see "Column types") in which to keep each row's summed weights at every level, as a column named as the weights, beside the value columns and not one of them: a reader that merges rows of one cell weights them by it (format version 4 in a file). Needs weights.

index

"json" (default) for set.json, or "parquet" for set.parquet, a shard table (format version 4; see a5_write_pyramid_set_table()).

compression

"snappy" (default), "zstd" or "none". hyparquet decodes snappy itself; zstd needs the hyparquet-compressors package in the browser.

metadata

Named character vector or list of strings to add to the file's key-value metadata, such as a renderer's settings as JSON. The keys "a5pyramid", "a5_index" and "ARROW:schema" are reserved.

threads

Number of threads, or NULL (default) for a5pyramid_threads().

Value

dest, invisibly.

Tiers and shards

The LODs are split into tiers, each a range of LODs with a shard resolution. A cell of a tier belongs to the shard keyed by the cell at the shard resolution containing its centre (a5R::a5_cell_to_supercell()), so every cell is in exactly one shard. Each shard is one file holding its tier's LODs for the cells it owns, at tier=<t>/shard=<cell>.parquet. The levels are built from all the leaves before the pyramid is split, so a coarse cell near a shard's edge summarises every leaf under it, whichever shard holds them.

a5_pyramid_set_tiers() gives the default tiers: three LODs a tier from the leaves down, each keyed 12 resolutions coarser than its finest LOD, and the remaining LODs in one tier keyed at resolution 0. A shard full of data then holds about 22 million rows, and a map view meets at most a few shards of the tier it draws at any zoom.

Files

A shard is an a5pyramid file in format version 2: as a file from a5_write_pyramid(), with the index also recording the shard, and with data_resolution the leaves' resolution even in shards of coarser tiers. a5_pyramid_info() and a5_read_pyramid() read shards. A shard can hold no cells at some LOD of its tier, never at all of them; shards without cells are not written. set.json lists the tiers and every shard with its path, rows, tiles, size, footer size and bounding box, and is written last, so a set with an index is complete. A write that fails or is interrupted removes the shards it wrote, and dest if it created it, so it can be run again. The format is specified in FORMAT.md in the package source.

See also

a5_pyramid_set_info() to read the index, a5_write_pyramid() for a single file.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
x <- data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells)))

dest <- tempfile()
tiers <- data.frame(
  lod_min = c(2, 13), lod_max = c(12, 15),
  shard_resolution = c(0, 10), tile_size = c(4096, 4096)
)
a5_write_pyramid_set(x, dest, tiers = tiers)
info <- a5_pyramid_set_info(dest)
info
